title: What If You Could See Infrared Light? Volunteers Did

scenes.text: What if you could see light you're built to miss? In one lab, thirty volunteers did.
Human eyes normally see wavelengths from about 400 to 720 nanometers. Infrared sits beyond that.
Scientists pulsed infrared lasers at the eye, and the retina absorbed two photons at once.
Two photons together carry the energy of one visible photon. The brain read it as normal light.
All thirty volunteers saw lasers at 950 to 1,200 nanometers, and they looked like a pale green glow.
So infrared vision isn't impossible. The light is just too weak, unless you pulse it hard.
